_about: Banks for the tavern generator. Prices are in gp (0.1 = 1 silver piece, 0.01 = 1 copper). Edit freely; {place}, {faction}, {npc}, {church} and {owner} are filled in when a tavern is generated.

kinds.name: Dockside tavern
outside: A sagging timber building on stilts over the water, its sign a painted anchor.
Wedged between two warehouses, with a door so low everyone ducks.
A converted boathouse, the old slipway now a beer garden.
A tarred plank shack with an upturned boat for a roof.
A stone cellar under the fish market, reached by slimy steps.
A former customs house, its official sign painted over with a leaping fish.
A long, low shed hung with drying nets, its door propped open with an anchor.
A ship's hull hauled ashore and fitted with windows, still named for the ship.
inside: Sawdust on the floor, nets on the ceiling, and a smell of tar and fried fish.
Long benches, scarred tables and a fire that smokes more than it warms.
Low beams hung with lanterns, and a floor that rocks slightly when the tide comes in.
Lanterns made from fish-oil jars throw greasy yellow light over a crowd of dockhands.
A bar made of a ship's mast laid on barrels, polished smooth by a thousand elbows.
Tables nailed to the floor, as if the room expects a storm.
A chalkboard of ships due in and out, and bets on which will be late.
Salt crusts the windows; inside it is warm, loud and smells of wet rope.
patrons: dockhands
fishers
sailors on shore leave
smugglers pretending to be sailors
off-duty harbour guards
a cargo master counting coins under the table
pearl divers still wet from the harbour
a press gang looking for sailors who've had one too many

kinds.name: Roadside inn
outside: A long stone inn with stables, a well and a sign creaking in the wind.
A whitewashed coaching inn at a crossroads, its yard full of carts.
A fortified inn with a wooden palisade, built for monster country.
A coaching inn with a yard full of wagons and a farrier hammering at the side.
A fortified waystation with a ditch, a palisade and a very small door.
A rambling farmhouse that turned into an inn one room at a time.
A stone inn at a crossroads, its sign shot full of arrows by bored travellers.
A long thatched building beside a ford, with a bell to call the ferryman.
inside: A wide common room with a hearth big enough to roast a pig, and usually does.
Clean rushes on the floor, polished tables and a cat on every windowsill.
A cosy room of dark wood, with a notice board crowded with travellers' messages.
A hearth big enough to roast an ox, and an ox roasting in it.
Benches packed with travellers trading road news over bowls of the same stew.
A common room with a map of the region painted on one wall, travellers' corrections scratched into it.
Low ceilings, smoked hams hanging from the beams, and a dog asleep under every table.
A quiet room upstairs for those who pay extra, and a noisy one downstairs for those who don't.
patrons: merchants on the road
a caravan's guards
pilgrims
farmers come to sell at market
a courier changing horses
a tinker with a cart full of pots
a family moving house with everything they own
a Society courier eating standing up

kinds.name: Adventurers' haunt
outside: A rowdy hall across the street from the Adventure Society, its door propped open.
A tall building with a monster skull nailed above the door.
An old guardhouse turned tavern, still with arrow slits.
A squat stone hall beside the Society building, its door studded with old monster teeth.
A tavern with a mounted monster head over the door, its eyes replaced with lanterns.
A former armoury, the old weapon racks now holding patrons' gear.
A tall wooden building with a contract board of its own outside, for jobs too odd for the Society.
A hall with team banners hanging from every window.
inside: Trophies on every wall, each with a bragging plaque.
A contract board by the bar, and a corner where teams recruit.
A sparring ring in the back where disagreements get settled.
Every wall holds a trophy, each with a brass plate naming the team and the day.
A ranking board behind the bar, with the house's own rules for who's best this season.
A healer's corner in the back where cuts are stitched between drinks.
Long tables claimed by teams, and a strict rule against sitting at another team's table.
A bell above the bar that's rung for every team that comes back from an astral space whole.
patrons: Iron-rank adventurers celebrating their first contract
a Bronze-rank team arguing over loot
a Society official off duty
would-be adventurers looking for a team
a healer patching up a broken arm at the bar
a team celebrating their first Bronze contract
a retired Gold-ranker who drinks alone and listens
a nervous Normal-rank kid trying to join any team

kinds.name: Noble wine hall
outside: A marble frontage with a doorman who looks at your boots before your face.
A walled garden hall lit by floating lanterns.
A converted townhouse with stained glass windows bearing house crests.
A glasshouse full of orange trees, with tables set between them.
A townhouse with no sign at all; the right people know which door.
A riverside pavilion reached by a private jetty, lanterns on the water.
A tall house with liveried footmen who announce each guest by name.
An arcade of shops, and at its end a wine hall with a carved stone vine over the arch.
inside: Velvet booths, a string quartet and wine poured by the thimble.
Private alcoves behind curtains, and a host who remembers every name.
Mirrored walls, gilded chairs and conversation kept at a polite murmur.
Silver bells on each table to summon a servant; nobody raises their voice.
Portraits of famous patrons, some of whom are in the room, ageing badly beside their pictures.
A gallery above where musicians play, unseen, so as not to distract from conversation.
Card tables in a side room where fortunes change hands under a painted ceiling.
A sommelier who describes each wine at length, and a guest who's clearly heard it before.
patrons: minor nobles
wealthy merchants
a Silver-rank adventurer who is pretending not to be noticed
a Storm Kingdom envoy meeting someone in secret
a noble house's heir with too much money
a poet paid to be witty
a matchmaker working three tables at once
a magistrate who shouldn't be seen here

kinds.name: Dive
outside: A cellar bar under a pawnshop, reached by a stair that smells of old ale.
An unmarked door with a lantern hung beside it, and a bruiser who decides who enters.
A shack at the edge of the slums with a hand-painted sign.
A door in an alley with no sign, just a painted eye.
A cellar under a tannery; the smell is a feature, not a flaw.
A half-burned building that never closed during the fire.
A shack built against the city wall, its roof patched with stolen tiles.
A former chapel, its pews now benches and its altar a bar.
inside: Dim, smoky and loud, with sticky tables and a dice game in every corner.
A single long bar and a lot of people trying not to be remembered.
Cramped, hot and cheerful, with a bard who plays for drinks.
One table, one barrel, one rule: no questions.
Sawdust over the stains and fresh stains over the sawdust.
A fighting pit in the middle of the room, with a bet board chalked on the wall.
A room so dark the barkeep hands out candles at the door.
Drinks served in chipped cups that don't match, from a barrel that has no label.
patrons: dice players
thieves between jobs
labourers spending the day's wages
a fence doing business at the back table
someone hiding from {faction}
a fence with a coat full of pockets
an off-duty watchman pretending he isn't one
a fighter with fresh stitches looking for the man who caused them
a gang of dock thieves
a broke adventurer selling their last core

kinds.name: Temple hostel
outside: A plain hostel attached to a shrine of {church}, open to all travellers.
A walled courtyard with a fountain, run by acolytes of {church}.
A plain stone guesthouse beside the temple, with a bowl of water by the door for travellers' feet.
A cloister wing opened to pilgrims, with a quiet garden at its heart.
A long hall built from donated timber, each beam carved with a donor's name.
A wayhouse with the church's symbol painted bright over the door.
A converted granary, its upper floor lined with straw beds for pilgrims.
inside: Simple wooden tables, a long communal meal and a prayer before eating.
Quiet halls, clean beds, and no drinking after the evening bell.
Long tables where everyone eats the same simple meal after a short prayer.
Quiet rules painted on the wall, and a novice who enforces them with a look.
A shrine in the corner where travellers leave small gifts for safe roads.
Shared dormitories, a curtain between each bed, and the smell of incense.
A healing room where priests tend the sick for whatever they can pay.
patrons: pilgrims
the sick hoping for healing
acolytes of {church}
a penitent noble
travellers too poor for an inn

kinds.name: Village alehouse
outside: A thatched cottage with a bush tied over the door to show there's ale.
The front room of the miller's house, open in the evenings.
A cottage with a broom over the door to show the ale is ready.
A barn with its doors thrown open and benches set out on the green.
A mill house that brews on the side and doesn't tell the lord.
A small stone house by the well, the only building in the village with two floors.
A tumbledown cottage with a garden of hops climbing the walls.
inside: One room, one fire, one barrel, and everyone in the village knows each other.
Benches by the fire, a dog asleep on someone's feet, and a slow game of cards.
One room, one fire, and everyone in the village in it by sunset.
A brewing vat in the corner, and the brewer's children asleep behind it.
Notices about lost sheep, a wedding and a wolf pinned to the door.
A single long table, where newcomers are expected to sit with strangers.
Walls hung with farm tools, and a fiddler who plays the same three tunes.
patrons: farmers
the village elder
a hunter back from the woods
a travelling tinker
a nervous young person dreaming of becoming an adventurer

kinds.name: River barge
outside: A broad flat barge moored at the quay, with a painted awning over the deck.
A string of three barges lashed together, the middle one a kitchen.
A barge that travels the river and ties up at a different town each tenday.
A barge with a garden on its roof and a goat that lives there.
An old grain barge with lanterns strung from its mast.
inside: A low cabin where the floor sways and the drinks slide.
Benches along the gunwales and a fire pit in an iron tub.
A deck open to the stars, with nets hung to stop drunks going overboard.
Cabins below for sleeping, each smaller than a wardrobe.
A captain who also cooks, and won't let anyone else near the stove.
patrons: river traders
a family of fishers
a smuggler waiting for a signal from the bank
pilgrims heading downstream
a Magic Society scholar studying the river

kinds.name: Caravanserai
outside: A square fortress of mud brick around a courtyard, with one great gate shut at sunset.
A ring of stone arches around a well, with camels kneeling in the shade.
A walled compound with a watchtower and a banner showing which guild owns it.
A sprawling stable and inn at the edge of the desert road, its walls painted with route maps.
A domed building with wind towers that keep it cool in the heat.
inside: Merchants from a dozen places trade around the well, haggling in three languages.
Upper rooms for travellers, lower rooms for animals and goods, and a guard on every stair.
Carpets on the floor, cushions instead of chairs, and mint tea poured from a great height.
A courtyard kitchen where every caravan cooks its own food, and everyone tastes everyone's.
A quiet hall where deals are sealed with a handshake and a witness.
patrons: caravan masters
camel drivers
a spice merchant with sample jars
a steppe clan rider trading horses
a Society team guarding a caravan

kinds.name: Gambling den
outside: A respectable-looking teahouse with a back door that gets more use than the front.
A tall house with shuttered windows and the sound of dice through every shutter.
A floating hall on the river, lit with red lanterns.
A warehouse with a doorman who asks for a password and accepts any coin as one.
A dance hall upstairs and a card room downstairs.
inside: Card tables, dice tables and a wheel that spins a little too freely.
A cage where coin is changed for chips, and a guard with a crossbow behind it.
Velvet curtains, cheap wine and a house that always wins.
A betting board for monster fights held in the yard behind.
A quiet room for high-stakes games, with its own door and its own guards.
patrons: a noble's son losing his inheritance
a card sharp with too many aces
a debt collector watching the tables
a lucky farmer who can't stop winning
an adventurer betting on their own next contract

food: Fish stew with too much pepper
Roast monster haunch (the cook won't say which monster)
Spiced rice with dates and almonds
Mushroom pie from the deep forest
A whole roast bird for the table to share
drink: Dwarven-style lager from the hill country
Small beer for the children and the careful
Bitter herbal liqueur, said to settle the stomach
Sparkling white for those who're paying
Barley wine that's stronger than it tastes
Smoked tea from the northern coasts
Sweet cider with a cinnamon stick
special: Coinfire brandy, distilled with a crushed iron spirit coin. Essence users feel a warm buzz; anyone else gets a headache.
Kraken ink rum. Turns your tongue black for a day.
Astral honey mead, from bees kept near an astral space. Tastes of flowers that don't exist.
The Widow-Maker, a chilli stew. Finishing it earns a free drink and your name on the wall.
Glowcap ale, faintly luminous. Harmless, mostly.
Monster-egg custard, from a nest the owner raided personally.
A cup of something the house calls 'Liquid Courage'. Advantage on one save against fear in the next hour, then disadvantage on Wisdom checks until you sleep.
Storm-cellar stout, aged in a barrel struck by lightning. Your hair stands up while you drink it.
A plate of tiny pies, each with a different filling, and one with a lucky coin inside.
Ice wine chilled with a sliver of a frost elemental's core. Breath steams for an hour.
The owner's grandmother's soup. Nobody knows the recipe. Everybody comes back for it.
Ember peppers stuffed with goat cheese. Fire affinity patrons swear they taste sweet.
A glass of wine from a bottle older than the city. One glass only, per patron, per year.
Salt-crusted fish cooked in a pit of coals in the yard, served whole for the table.
A mug of 'Fresh Start', a sobering tea that clears the head in minutes and tastes of regret.
Sweet rice dumplings in syrup, served at midnight only.
Monster-jerky board: six kinds, labelled with the monster and the team that brought it in.
Spirit-coin tea, steeped with a copper coin. Faintly restorative to essence users; useless to anyone else.
A shared pot of chilli so hot the house keeps a healer on hand. Survivors drink free.
Candied river eels, a delta delicacy.

staff: a harried barkeep who never stops polishing the same mug
a cook who shouts from the kitchen but never comes out
a teenage server who knows every rumour in town
a bouncer with a monster-claw scar who speaks in a whisper
the owner's elderly parent, who sits by the fire and judges everyone
a bard on retainer who only knows sad songs
a server who is secretly an Iron-rank adventurer saving for gear
twins who run the bar and finish each other's sentences
a stable hand who sleeps in the hayloft and hears everything
a server who sings the orders instead of saying them
an owner who insists on shaking every patron's hand
a cellar keeper with a lantern and a nervous laugh
a retired soldier who keeps order with a look
a goblin cook who swears every dish is his grandmother's recipe
a quiet server who notices everything and writes it in a little book
a pot-boy who wants to be an adventurer and asks every team to take him
an elderly harpist who has played here for forty years
a doorman who insists on taking everyone's weapons and loses half of them
a barmaid with a divine essence who blesses the ale
a nervous new owner still learning the trade
a former noble's chef who looks down on everything she cooks
patronDetails: arguing loudly about {faction}
playing a dice game with suspiciously good luck
nursing one drink all night and watching the door
celebrating a birthday with too much noise
trying to sell a map to anyone who'll listen
asleep face-down on the table
telling a tall tale about a monster in {place}
writing a letter and crying a little
looking for a team to take a contract
comparing essence abilities and showing off
betting on an arm-wrestling match
quietly praying to {church} over their meal
complaining about the price of awakening stones
asking everyone if they've seen {npc}
sharpening a blade at the table
teaching a card game with rules that change every hand
loudly describing a surgery in detail
reading a Society notice aloud to friends who can't read
drawing everyone in the room in charcoal
quietly selling awakening stones from a pouch
insisting the party sit with them
swearing they saw the duke in disguise last night
telling a story about an outworlder they met
trying to start a song nobody joins
practising a speech under their breath
picking a fight with the bard
watching the party a little too closely
feeding scraps to a monster pup under the table
arguing about which god is best
recruiting for a team going somewhere dangerous
entertainment: A bard sings an old ballad about the founding of {place}.
Arm-wrestling contest, winner takes the pot.
A storyteller performs the tale of an adventure team that never came back.
Dice tournament in the back room.
A travelling troupe performs a comedy mocking {faction}.
Nothing tonight but the fire and the rain.
A dancer from the delta performs with lit torches.
A magic show by an Iron-rank illusionist who is very proud of their essence.
Open stage night. Anyone brave enough can perform.
A drinking contest that the owner very much regrets allowing.
Two bards are duelling in verse, each insulting the other's mother.
A puppet show retelling a famous monster hunt, with the monster played by a sock.
Card tournament with a pot of spirit coins.
A fortune teller reads palms at the corner table, and gets a few uncomfortably right.
An outworlder sings a song from their home world nobody understands but everyone enjoys.
A storytelling contest; the best lie wins a free room.
A drummer and a fiddler who can't agree on the tune.
A wrestling match between the cook and a farmer, for reasons nobody will explain.
A choir from the local church practising for the holy day, badly.
A monster-fighting demonstration by a Bronze-ranker with a stuffed dummy and a very real sword.
A traveller shows a magic lantern that throws pictures of far places on the wall.
Dancing, with the tables pushed back and everyone expected to join.
An Iron-rank team takes bets on whether their healer can heal a drunk faster than he can drink.
Quiet tonight: a funeral wake for a regular, and toasts in their memory.
events: A brawl breaks out between two adventuring teams over a contract.
A stranger collapses at the door, wounded, clutching a monster core.
Guards arrive asking questions about someone who was here an hour ago.
The bard dedicates the next song to the party, and it is clearly about them. It is not flattering.
Someone pays for a round for the whole room, then slips out the back without paying.
A cat knocks a lantern into the straw, and the corner catches fire.
A messenger arrives with a letter addressed to one of the party by name.
The cellar door bangs from below, though the owner swears nobody is down there.
A noble's servant offers the party a job, with payment up front.
An adventurer's familiar escapes and starts stealing food from every table.
The floor trembles. A monster surge in the area, and everyone looks at the adventurers.
A drunk patron insists one of the party owes them money from a past they don't remember.
A Society clerk bursts in to say a surge has been sighted and every team must report.
The owner announces the place is closing for good tomorrow, and the room goes very quiet.
A pickpocket is caught in the act and begs the party for help.
A wedding party arrives, already drunk, and takes over the room.
The floor gives way under the bar, revealing a cellar no one knew about.
A famous adventurer walks in, and three people faint.
A child brings in a monster egg they found and asks what it is. It's starting to crack.
A noble insists on the party's table and offers coin to move.
The lanterns flicker blue for a moment, and every essence user feels a chill.
A messenger bird lands on the bar with a note tied to its leg, addressed to no one.
A drunk challenges the toughest-looking party member to a duel.
The rain turns to hail, and the whole street crams inside.
A man in chains bursts through the door, closely followed by the watch.
The owner's prize pig gets loose in the common room.
A priest arrives to bless the building, and finds something in it that doesn't want blessing.
Someone has spiked the ale with something that makes everyone tell the truth.
The bard plays a song and someone in the room starts crying, then runs out.
A group of masked figures enter, look around, and leave without a word.
Someone falls ill after eating the special. Was it the food or someone's poison?
A Silver-rank team stops by to recruit, and they're interested in the party.
An old woman insists a party member is her long-lost grandchild.
Every door in the building swings shut at once.
A monster core rolls across the floor from nowhere and stops at the party's feet.
The watch announces a curfew, starting now.
Two teams agree to settle a dispute with an arm-wrestling match and the room clears a table.
A visiting merchant offers to buy the tavern on the spot.
A mysterious stranger pays for the party's drinks and leaves before they can thank her.
The fire in the hearth turns green and starts to speak.
rumours: A team from the Adventure Society went into an astral space near {place} three days ago and hasn't come out.
{npc} has been drinking here every night this week and leaving huge tips. Where's the money coming from?
The price of cores has doubled since {faction} started buying them up.
There's something big in the water past the harbour wall. The fishers won't go out.
A priest of {church} is offering divine essences to anyone who'll work their fields.
Someone's been selling fake awakening stones; they work once and then crumble.
A noble house is quietly hiring adventurers for a job they won't discuss in writing.
Strange lights have been seen over {place} at night, the kind that come before a surge.
The owner used to be an adventurer and still has their essence. Don't start trouble.
A cult is recruiting in the poor quarter, promising essences to anyone who joins.
The Magic Society paid a fortune for a dead monster last week and won't say why.
There's a reward for information on whoever robbed the coin farm outside {place}.
The Magic Society is quietly buying land around {place}. Nobody knows why.
There's a new astral space in the old quarry, and it's leaking cold air.
A merchant in {place} has been selling cores that aren't monster cores at all.
The duke's steward has a gambling problem and a lot of debts.
Someone saw a ship with black sails off the coast, flying no flag.
{npc} has been seen meeting with people from {faction} after dark.
A healer at the temple can cure anything, for a price no one will name.
The last team that went into the marsh came back with one more member than they left with.
There's going to be a new tax on essences, and the Society is furious.
A child in {place} was born with a mark that matches an old prophecy.
The well water's turned salty in three villages this month.
An outworlder turned up in {place} speaking a language no one understands.
{church} is quarrelling with {faction} over a plot of land and someone is going to get hurt.
A new cult is recruiting from the orphanages, offering food and a family.
The road north is safe now; something killed the bandits there. Something big.
A Gold-ranker is in town, and she's asking questions about an old contract.
There's a monster in the sewers that the watch won't admit exists.
Someone's been buying all the silver in {place}, in small amounts, from every smith.
The bridge at {place} is being torn down, and people are angry about it.
The noble houses are arranging a marriage that could change everything.
The harvest has failed upriver and prices are going to climb.
A ghost walks the old battlefield every full moon, looking for its sword.
Someone stole a whole statue from the temple square, overnight, without a sound.
The Adventure Society is going to raise the price of rank assessments.
A boatload of refugees arrived from across the sea with stories of a war.
A traveller paid for a room with a coin from no known mint.
The old lighthouse keeper says he saw a sea serpent, and nobody laughed this time.
There's a buyer in {place} who pays triple for monster eggs.
hooks: The owner offers free rooms for a week if the party clears out whatever is living in the cellar.
A patron offers 3 bronze spirit coins to escort them to {place} at dawn, no questions.
A note under the party's tankard reads: 'Meet me at the docks at midnight. Come armed.'
The bard wants the party to take them on an adventure, for material.
A crying child asks the party to find their parent, who went to sell cores and didn't come home.
The owner owes money to {faction} and asks the party to negotiate on their behalf.
An old adventurer offers a map to an astral space in exchange for one last drink and a promise.
A server asks the party to deliver a package to {npc}, and not to open it.
A patron hands the party a key and dies before they can say what it opens.
The owner asks the party to find out who keeps stealing the silverware, one spoon a night.
A Society clerk off duty asks the party to look into a contract that went wrong, unofficially.
A widow wants to hire the party to find her husband's killer; the watch has given up.
A merchant offers to pay for the party's meal if they'll test his new monster-repellent.
A young noble wants lessons in being an adventurer, and will pay well.
A tired priest asks the party to escort a relic to a shrine, tomorrow.
An old map pinned behind the bar has an X on it that the owner swears is real.
The barkeep slides over a note: someone at the corner table wants the party dead.
A stranger offers a bet: spend one night in the haunted room upstairs and win a purse of coins.
Two teams want the party to settle their dispute, and both will pay for the 'right' verdict.
A child sells a 'magic' pebble that turns out to be an awakening stone.
A farmer asks for help with a monster nobody believes exists.
A traveller asks the party to deliver a letter to their sister in another city.
A Magic Society researcher wants volunteers for a harmless experiment. Probably harmless.
A notorious smuggler wants to hire guards for one night, no questions, very good money.
The cook's kitchen has a door that wasn't there yesterday.
The owner's daughter has run off with an adventurer; the owner wants her back, or at least a letter.
An outworlder recognises something on a party member and asks where they got it.
A local hero challenges the party to a contest of strength, with the town watching.
A cult symbol is carved under the party's table. It's fresh.
The bard is writing an epic and needs a dragon. The party knows where to find one.
A beggar offers information about a theft for the price of a meal.
A noble's lost dog has wandered in, and its collar holds a ransom note.
A scholar wants an escort to the ruins outside {place}, leaving at dawn.
A drunk insists he's the rightful heir to a noble house and has proof in a box he buried.
The owner needs supplies from a farm cut off by a monster, and will pay in free board.
A retired adventurer wants to sell the party their old team's equipment, cursed or not.
A merchant's caravan leaves tomorrow, and its guards just quit.
Someone at the bar is wearing a party member's stolen cloak.
A messenger has the wrong name but the right description: the party is wanted somewhere.
A woman asks the party to fake her death.
secrets: The cellar connects to the smugglers' tunnels under {place}. The owner takes a cut.
The owner is an informant for {faction} and passes on anything adventurers let slip.
A cult meets in the back room every new moon, and the owner pretends not to know.
The house special contains a monster ingredient that is slowly addictive.
One of the staff is a fugitive outworlder hiding under a false name.
The owner's divine essence was granted by {church}, and the church expects favours in return.
The tavern was won in a card game, and the previous owner wants it back, badly.
A dead adventurer's essence is hidden in a loose stone behind the hearth. The owner doesn't know it's there.
The rooms upstairs are sometimes rented by the hour to people meeting in secret, and the owner keeps a ledger of who.
The ale is watered and the wine is worse, and the owner pays a priest to say nothing.
The owner was once a Silver-rank adventurer who faked their own death.
There's a body walled up in the cellar, and the cellar knows it.
The back room is a meeting place for {faction}, who pay well for discretion.
One of the regulars is a doppelganger who replaced the real one last winter.
The cook is poisoning one patron, slowly, at someone's request.
The tavern is built on top of an astral space that opens once a decade. The next opening is close.
The owner sells patrons' gossip to a gossip sheet.
The staircase hides a vault full of stolen essences.
The owner is heavily in debt and plans to burn the place down for the insurance.
A ghost lives in the attic, and the owner leaves it a drink every night.
The bard is a spy from the Storm Kingdom.
The tavern's sign is an awakening stone set in wood; nobody realises.
One of the rooms has a spyhole, and the owner rents it to a blackmailer.
The owner's spouse is a cultist who uses the tavern to choose recruits.
A noble house secretly owns the tavern and uses it to watch a rival.
The place was cursed by a wronged patron: no one born here can leave for long.
The well in the yard is connected to the river through a cave where smugglers hide goods.
The famous house special uses an ingredient that's illegal in the city.
The owner pays protection to a gang, and the gang wants more.
The staff are all ex-convicts, given a second chance, and loyal to the owner to a fault.
A child's room upstairs belongs to a child who disappeared years ago, and the owner keeps it ready.
The cellar holds a monster the owner is raising as a pet, and it's getting big.

events
A Society clerk bursts in to say a surge has been sighted and every team must report.
The owner announces the place is closing for good tomorrow, and the room goes very quiet.
A pickpocket is caught in the act and begs the party for help.
A wedding party arrives, already drunk, and takes over the room.
The floor gives way under the bar, revealing a cellar no one knew about.
A famous adventurer walks in, and three people faint.
A child brings in a monster egg they found and asks what it is. It's starting to crack.
A noble insists on the party's table and offers coin to move.
The lanterns flicker blue for a moment, and every essence user feels a chill.
A messenger bird lands on the bar with a note tied to its leg, addressed to no one.
A drunk challenges the toughest-looking party member to a duel.
The rain turns to hail, and the whole street crams inside.
A man in chains bursts through the door, closely followed by the watch.
The owner's prize pig gets loose in the common room.
A priest arrives to bless the building, and finds something in it that doesn't want blessing.
Someone has spiked the ale with something that makes everyone tell the truth.
The bard plays a song and someone in the room starts crying, then runs out.
A group of masked figures enter, look around, and leave without a word.
Someone falls ill after eating the special. Was it the food or someone's poison?
A Silver-rank team stops by to recruit, and they're interested in the party.
An old woman insists a party member is her long-lost grandchild.
Every door in the building swings shut at once.
A monster core rolls across the floor from nowhere and stops at the party's feet.
The watch announces a curfew, starting now.
Two teams agree to settle a dispute with an arm-wrestling match and the room clears a table.
A visiting merchant offers to buy the tavern on the spot.
A mysterious stranger pays for the party's drinks and leaves before they can thank her.
The fire in the hearth turns green and starts to speak.
